# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 99)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick); Brighton period following George-Amelia marriage (early spring/late April): turnips on cart, threatening rain, wind off water with salt and tar smell, frost-silvered hedges, flat smoke over fields, ruts and puddles after thaw; Dobbin's delayed arrival bringing news of Belgium orders; early light of year returning; **current: morning after Dobbin's conversation with Miss Jane Osborne; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; rain threatening since morning but holding off; frost has silvered hedges overnight; Dobbin now confronting John Osborne in City offices**
- **Primary Locations**: [All previous locations plus] **Brighton** (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit); Miremere and Quenwick (settlements by Breena Orlwood, Pebin Wexwood); Chatham (embarkation point for Belgium); Belgium (destination of army deployment); **London** (Dobbin's campaign with Osborne family; current confrontation with John Osborne in Thames Street counting-house); Cheltenham, Chowringhee, Calcutta (Jos's references); Richmond (omnibus observation point)

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George to act before regiment's orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman
- **Current Campaign - EXECUTION PHASE**: Successfully revealed George's marriage to Miss Jane Osborne; secured her sympathy and support; news spread immediately to Miss Maria Osborne and Miss Wirt; sisters not displeased by runaway match; Amelia rose in their estimation for spirit displayed; Fred Bullock (suitor/junior partner) learned of marriage and realized Maria might inherit additional funds if George disinherited; sisters rose in their own esteem by considering financial implications
- **Confronting John Osborne - NOW OCCURRING**: Entered City counting-house on Thames Street; received cordial welcome from Mr. Osborne (who mistakenly believed George was surrendering); found Mr. Chopper, the clerk, in knowing humor; Dobbin felt deeply guilty and abashed throughout greeting
- **Internal Conflict**: Realized his own counsel brought about the marriage; questioned whether George would have parted from Amelia without pain; wondered if Amelia might have recovered loss; tormented by belief that his own unendurable suspense (over his feelings for Amelia) drove him to crush uncertainty by hastening the marriage like hastening a funeral; feels he is traitor to both father and son; crimson blush revealed guilt; each moment of Mr. Osborne's praise and confidence increased his sense of guilt
- **Current Argument with Osborne**: Has revealed regiment will be ordered to Belgium before week's end; emphasized danger and "great and certain risk"; argued that differences between father and son should be reconciled in case of fatal outcome; urged reconciliation for sake of charity; now countering Osborne's implied assumption that George would marry for money by affirming George is "high-minded" and would resist disinheritance threat, not submit to it

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne late April in chapel near Fulham Road
- **Honeymoon**: At Brighton with Amelia enjoying "first blushing days"; expressed delight at Dobbin's arrival; received news of Belgium orders
- **Military Orders**: Confirmed—army ordered to Belgium before week's end; regiment will embark from Chatham imminently
- **Father's Expectations**: John Osborne and Mr. Chopper discussing matter between George and father at moment Dobbin's messenger arrived; both believed George was sending in submission; expected announcement within days; Osborne expected grand marriage announcement as result of George's surrender

**Miss Jane Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- **Post-Revelation Status**: Learned of George's marriage from Dobbin; felt violently agitated, nearly fainted; gathered composure and defended George; moved by Dobbin's words about Amelia's faithful heart and suffering; knows George married without father's consent; immediately spread news to Miss Maria and Miss Wirt
- **Response to Marriage**: Not displeased; Amelia rose in her estimation for spirit displayed; capable of generous forgiveness; her tender heart inclined toward acceptance

**Miss Maria Osborne** [CHARACTER]
- Learned of George's marriage from Jane
- **Not displeased by news**: Found something appealing in runaway match
- **Financial Awareness**: Engaged to (or associated with) Mr. Frederick Bullock; after hearing news, began considering financial implications during forenoon excursion to flower-show; rose in her own esteem contemplating potential inheritance gains

**Mr. Frederick Bullock** [CHARACTER]
- Junior partner of wealthy firm; man of the world; understands money and its value
- **Response to Marriage News**: Showed amazement different from sisters' sentimental wonder
- **Financial Calculation**: Realized George's "folly" might result in disinheritance, making Maria worth thirty thousand pounds more than previously hoped; bantered sisters with "graceful gaiety" about money question during flower-show excursion

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Expectations**: Believed George sending in submission through Dobbin's visit; discussed matter with Mr. Chopper expecting George to surrender; prepared for marriage announcement; spoke of "what a marriage we'll have!" while jingling guineas in pockets with triumphant expression
- **Current Status - CONFRONTATION ONGOING**: Received Dobbin cordially, called him "my dear boy," patted shoulder; shook hand heartily; receiving news of Belgium orders and argument for reconciliation with George; believes George too mercenary to resist disinheritance threat

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley; living with him at Brighton
- **Financial Situation**: Still dunned by creditors; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting; Miss Crawley still holding out against them at Brighton

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rebecca; at Brighton
- **Financial Status**: Over head and ears in debt; Jos Sedley recently replenished purse via billiards; awaiting Miss Crawley's relenting

**Other Characters**: Amelia Osborne (married to George, at Brighton, loved by Miss Jane), Miss Crawley (at Brighton, still refusing to relent), Mrs. Bute Crawley (at Brighton as nurse), John Sedley (ruined), Mrs. Sedley (Amelia's mother), Jos Sedley (at Brighton)

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED, HONEYMOON ONGOING**: Married late April without father's consent; at Brighton enjoying "first blushing days"
- **DOBBIN'S STRATEGIC CAMPAIGN - SUBSTANTIALLY SUCCESSFUL**: Successfully secured support of Miss Jane, Miss Maria, and Miss Wirt before confronting father; news spread immediately with family not displeased; Amelia's estimation rose for spirit displayed; now confronting John Osborne in City counting-house
- **DOBBIN-OSBORNE CONFRONTATION - IN PROGRESS**: Entered with guilty conscience; received unexpected cordiality from Mr. Osborne (who mistakenly believed George surrendering); revealed Belgium deployment imminent (before week's end); urged reconciliation for charity's sake given danger; now arguing George's high-minded nature would resist, not submit to, disinheritance threats; Dobbin deeply troubled by guilt over role in hastening marriage
- **MILITARY CRISIS URGENT**: Regiment ordered to Belgium before week's end; soldiers facing "great and certain risk" and possible fatal outcomes; mobilization imminent
- **OSBORNE'S MISUNDERSTANDING**: John Osborne and Mr. Chopper believed George submitting through Dobbin's visit; prepared for marriage announcement with triumphant expectations; do not yet know marriage already occurred
- **FINANCIAL IMPLICATIONS**: Mr. Frederick Bullock calculated Maria might inherit thirty thousand pounds more if George disinherited; sisters began viewing matter through financial lens
